card: Modifies standard transaction relay policy to permit Taproot annexes that are marker-only (0x50) or unstructured data prefixed with 0x50 0x00. Currently, any Taproot transaction containing an annex is rejected as non-standard by default mempools. To protect multi-party transactions against unilateral annex introduction, the rule requires all non-P2A inputs to carry an annex if any input does. The PR revisits concepts from closed PR 27926 and Libre Relay, but cites no external issues or user demand.
evidence: Commit aa85bd97d1: 'Permit marker-only annexes and annexes whose first byte after the 0x50 marker is 0x00, reserving other prefixes for future semantics.'
problem: Transactions with Taproot annexes are currently treated as non-standard by Bitcoin Core and rejected from standard mempools, preventing users from relaying transactions that attach unstructured data or use marker-based opt-in semantics in Taproot witnesses.

risk.why: Mistakes in standardness policy could expose multi-party transactions to witness inflation attacks or partition mempools across the P2P network.

scope_notes: The diff was not provided. The PR is marked as draft and the description notes AI-assisted implementation and testing.
summary: Modifies mempool standardness policy to permit Taproot transactions with annexes if the annex is marker-only (0x50) or unstructured data prefixed with 0x50 0x00. Requires all non-P2A inputs in a transaction to include an annex if any input does, leaving other prefixes non-standard.
